a Phase-18 `PASS` is a bounded result over the corpus it drove, not a coverage or memory-safety claim: a site under a passing corpus is exercised by that corpus's classes, never proven safe
non_claims: a fuzzed site is on an attacker-input route a Phase-18 hostile-fuzz corpus drives, which is a bounded differential or property result over the corpus it drove: it is not a coverage claim about every input to the parser and not a memory-safety proof, so a site under a passing corpus is exercised by that corpus's classes, not proven safe

a Phase-18 verdict is about the corpus, not the site: a `PASS` says the corpus produced the observations it recorded (no crash, no OOM, no timeout over the entries it drove), never that a reachable unsafe site's contract holds

an unfuzzed site is recorded, not zeroed: a route no Phase-18 corpus drives carries an `evidence_missing` residual with its sites, and the census sites no attacker-input route reaches are `out_of_scope` because no fuzz target is expected to exercise them -- neither is a claim that the site is safe

the corpus is a fixed enumeration, not a coverage-guided fuzzer: the Phase-18 corpora and the bounded mutational screen are deterministic enumerations, so the absence of a finding is the absence of a finding over those bytes, never evidence that no input produces one

authority.declaration: the committed Phase-18 hostile-boundary register is the authority this plane reads: its surfaces name the hostile-fuzz courts, their corpus sizes and their candidate findings, the courts registry records the verdicts and the bounded mutational screen records the Phase-18 fuzz evidence; no verdict, corpus size or finding is typed here
authority.register_rule: This register is the stratum's own non-claims, recorded per surface as `hardened` (a change landed), `measured` (a passing court covers the surface) or `not-claimed` (explicitly outside this stratum). It is authored, not derived: the `HOSTILE-BOUNDARY-REGISTER` court in forensics/tools/phase18_courts.py re-reads the live courts registry and fails the stratum if any recorded classification, capacit

rule.mapping_rule: census unsafe site -> its 25.7 attacker-input route (the parser its committed module or authority unit is) -> the Phase-18 hostile-fuzz target whose surface group drives that input route
rule.partial_join: a partial join or a coverage gap is a residual, never a zero or a guess: an attacker-input route no Phase-18 corpus drives is `evidence_missing`, a register group that is not a fuzz target and the sites no attacker route reaches are `out_of_scope`, and a missing court record is `evidence_missing`

route_authority.rule: the attacker-input routes and the sites on them are the 25.7 exposure classification's own attacker_routes: a site is on a route when its committed module or authority unit is the parser the route names

rule.site_disposition: every routed census site is present in `.sites`: a `FUZZED` site names the Phase-18 targets that exercise it and its routes, and a `NOT_FUZZED` site names its routes and a closed reason; a site is never dropped
rule.sort_key: targets by name; sites by id; residuals by id; every list sorted
rule.target_disposition: every Phase-18 hostile-fuzz target is present in `.targets`: a target carries the sites on the routes its inputs drive, whether it is `covered`, its tool state (from the register verdict), its corpus size and its candidate findings; a target the register does not record is not invented

rows.note: a bounded, deterministic mutational screen over the committed hostile corpus, driven through the same probe the RT-HOSTILE-X509 court uses; NOT coverage-guided, NOT a fuzzing campaign, NOT a security proof
